correctness.rationale: Changed-position supports uniquely partition every distinct nonidentity output into swaps of unequal pairs at distance one or two, and two three-cycles on all-distinct consecutive triples. A two-state append transition counts each labeled input once and gives the claimed polynomial for every \(q\ge2\),\(n\ge3\). Conditional equality cases reconstruct mean, variance, and nonzero asymptotic variance; bounded two-dependent CLT applies. The sharp extrema follow from the local upper bound and the binary characteristic recurrence. Directly replayed exhaustive actual-output enumeration matched all claimed counts on 337673 words across 33 cases. Infinite statements depend on the proof, not these finite checks.

evidence: The primary theorem concerns asymptotic binary code redundancy; it derives only a mean sphere-size formula, not its complete distribution or finite variance.

A separate complete binary length-four substring-permutation population theorem concerns four-position permutations and cannot be specialized by alphabet or parameter substitution to an exact three-position q-ary distribution.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General k binary sphere-volume formulas do imply the elementary binary pointwise special case; they do not provide the q-ary three-cycle dynamics, its evaluated distribution and all-q moments. The new full claim is not a corollary of the stated prior conclusions.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected 2026 primary paper proves binary pointwise sphere-size enumeration for any window length and binary length-three correcting-code patterns, but does not state a q-ary two-state population polynomial, nonbinary three-cycle count, full variance or Gaussian law. A related binary length-four sphere population law does not imply the q-ary length-three law. The new theorem gives a complete finite-length distribution for every q, not just the inherited pointwise binary formula. Checked index records and targeted literature searches revealed no dominating q-ary treatment; risk of unindexed equivalent coverage is recorded.

value.rationale: The complete sphere-size population is a natural finite-block information-theoretic invariant of a recently studied permutation-burst channel: it gives the frequency of every ambiguity count rather than just a typical bound. The theorem captures \(q\ge3\) all-distinct three-cycles absent from binary work, reduces all alphabet sizes to a two-state weighted matrix, gives sharp extremizer multiplicities and quantitative typical fluctuations. These facts can calibrate sphere-packing and finite-length ensemble analyses, without a claim of improved code constructions.
